radar_fcs.tooltip.fcs: Controls the equipment of its radar network: CBC cannon mounts with aim controllers, Create: Radars radars, monitors, memory blocks. Needs power (FE). Right-click: settings and status; Shift+right-click: hold fire
radar_fcs.tooltip.transponder: Identification friend or foe. Right-click: code, zone mode (ship, radius, or ship and distance) and radius. Everything in the zone is friendly: mobs, players, vehicles, projectiles, ships. A fire control computer treats it as friendly if its code list (IFF tab) accepts the code. Needs power (FE). Dye only changes its color
radar_fcs.report.radar_missing: no working radar in the network
radar_fcs.tooltip.monitor: Shows targets from the Create: Radars radars of its radar network: friendly, hostile, inactive. Right-click a blip to designate it for the network's fire control computers (manual aiming); Shift+right-click opens the monitor window: target list, filters, scale. Build it as a wall. Needs power (FE): 32 FE/t per screen block
radar_fcs.status.no_power: no rotation on the aim controller
radar_fcs.report.spread: [CBC spread ±%s°: lengthen the barrel or use fewer charges]
radar_fcs.gui.title: Fire Control Computer
radar_fcs.gui.fire_hint.single: One shot, then a pause. Fires only when the predicted miss is within tolerance. The pause is in seconds; numbers change with the mouse wheel.
radar_fcs.gui.fire_hint.auto: Continuous fire while the predicted miss is within tolerance.
radar_fcs.gui.fire_hint.burst: A burst of the set length, then a pause. Counts projectiles that left the barrel. The pause is in seconds; numbers change with the mouse wheel.
radar_fcs.gui.targets_hint: Ships are Sable / Create Aeronautics structures; entities are Create contraptions, boats, minecarts and others (shells and rockets: Intercept tab). Priority level: higher comes first. Each target type has its own speed window, in m/s; "off" means no limit. Numbers change with the mouse wheel.
radar_fcs.gui.server_no_projectiles: The server forbids projectiles and rockets (allowProjectiles)
radar_fcs.gui.drop_hint: A dropped target is no longer engaged. Static means slower than the server's minSpeed for longer than the standing time (a short stop such as a turn does not count; a target that has never moved is static at once). Drop after N shots counts per gun: after its own N shots a gun leaves the target. Saving the settings brings dropped targets back.
radar_fcs.gui.pick_hint: The target type level comes first, then the priority mode. Each cannon picks its own target. Switching moves fire to another target and cycles through the ones left; with a single target, fire continues. A target designated on a monitor always comes first.
radar_fcs.tooltip.radar_link: Goes on a piece of equipment and adds it to a radar network, like a Create Stock Link. An untuned link starts a new network when placed; right-click a placed link to tune the item to its network. Unlimited range; a redstone signal of 15 disables it. Reset: Shift+right-click in the air or put it in a crafting grid
radar_fcs.link.not_linked: The link is not connected to a network
radar_fcs.tooltip.yaw_controller: Place directly under a CBC cannon mount and feed rotation from below. Turns the cannon horizontally by the needed angle; shaft speed sets the turn rate (256 RPM = 192°/s). Limit to the left and right of the mount's facing: slider on a side face (hold right-click), 1-360°, unlimited by default
radar_fcs.tooltip.pitch_controller: Place directly beside a CBC cannon mount and feed rotation from the other side. Elevates the barrel by the needed angle; shaft speed sets the rate. Limit up and down from the horizon: slider on a side face (hold right-click), unlimited by default
radar_fcs.controller.no_mount_yaw: No mount: place it directly under a CBC cannon mount
radar_fcs.controller.no_mount_pitch: No mount: place it directly beside a CBC cannon mount
radar_fcs.link.place_on_equipment: A radar link goes on equipment: computer, CBC mount, radar, monitor, memory block
radar_fcs.link.tooltip_untuned: Not tuned: starts a new network when placed. Right-click a placed link to join its network
radar_fcs.link.disabled: Radar network %s: link disabled by redstone
radar_fcs.link.network_info: Radar network %s: computers %s, cannons %s, radars %s, monitors %s, memory %s, cameras %s, camera monitors %s
radar_fcs.gui.hostile_only: Mobs: hostile only (passive ones via the whitelist)
radar_fcs.gui.lists_hint: Entry: entity ID (minecraft:cow), type tag (#minecraft:undead), every entity of a mod (create:*) or the name of a player, ship or name-tagged entity. Whitelist: always a target, even if its type is off or the mob is passive; blacklist: never. Friends by transponder and server limits take precedence over the lists.
radar_fcs.gui.assemble_hint: Assemble every cannon of this computer now; afterwards it keeps assembling them by itself
radar_fcs.gui.disassemble_hint: Disassemble every cannon of this computer (e.g. to reload or rebuild it); it will not assemble them until "Assemble" is pressed
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.title: Radar Monitor
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.no_radar: No Create: Radars radar in the monitor's network
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.coords: X %s Y %s Z %s, range %s m, height %s m, %s m/s
radar_fcs.gui.iff_mode_white: Mode: whitelist — only transponders with listed codes are friendly
radar_fcs.gui.iff_mode_black: Mode: blacklist — every transponder is friendly except listed codes
radar_fcs.gui.iff_hidden: Codes are hidden: only the computer's owner, their team and operators see and change them.
radar_fcs.gui.iff_hint_white: Whitelist: a transponder is friendly only if its code is listed; transponders without a code or with other codes are not friendly (they protect nothing). Enter the code in the transponder too (right-click it). The owner, their team and friendlyPlayers are always friendly.
radar_fcs.gui.iff_hint_black: Blacklist: every transponder (also without a code) is friendly except the listed codes — their zones and ships are not protected. Enter the code in the transponder too (right-click it). The owner, their team and friendlyPlayers are always friendly.
radar_fcs.msg.transponder_locked: Someone else's transponder: only the owner, their team and operators see and change its settings
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.title: IFF Transponder
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.mode.sublevel: Zone: the ship it stands on
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_sublevel: Friendly: the whole Sable / Create Aeronautics ship (or Create contraption) the transponder stands on and everything within it: mobs, players, vehicles, projectiles.
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_sublevel_: The transponder is not on a ship: in this mode it protects nothing. Put it on a ship or choose radius.
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_radius: Friendly: everything within the radius: mobs (hostile too), players, vehicles, contraptions, projectiles, ships. On a ship the ship itself is friendly too and the zone moves with it.
radar_fcs.tooltip.memory: Linked into a fire control computer's radar network, adds %s more entries to each of its lists (target whitelist and blacklist, IFF codes). Needs power (FE)
radar_fcs.memory.on: Memory block online: +%s entries to the lists of the network's computers
radar_fcs.memory.off: No power: the memory block needs %s FE/t
radar_fcs.report.no_energy: NO POWER: the computer needs %s FE/t
radar_fcs.report.memory: Memory: %s entries per list, memory blocks in the network: %s
radar_fcs.monitor.no_energy: No power: the monitor is off
radar_fcs.gui.list_no_memory: Inactive: not enough memory. Add a memory block to the network (+16 entries) or remove the entry
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.mode.sublevel_: Zone: ship and distance from it
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_combined: Friendly: the ship the transponder stands on and everything within the distance from its bounds: escorts, mobs, players, projectiles.
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.hint_combined_: The transponder is not on a ship: in this mode it protects a sphere of the given radius around itself.
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.name: Name
radar_fcs.transponder_gui.inherit_hint: Entry: entity ID (minecraft:villager), tag (#minecraft:raiders), every entity of a mod (create:*) or the name of a player, ship or name-tagged entity. "Always" inherits protection even if its type is off; "never" does not. The ship carrying the transponder is always friendly.
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.scope_hint: Hover over a blip for target details; click to designate it for the network's fire control computers (manual aiming), click again to clear; middle-click excludes the target from fire, again restores it (it is also restored when the target leaves radar coverage).
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.list_hint: Click: designate/clear; middle-click: exclude from fire/restore
radar_fcs.gui.impact_first: On equal level, first the projectile that will reach friendlies sooner
radar_fcs.gui.intercept_no_mod: Without it CBC projectiles pass through each other, so interception is off: guns do not aim or fire at shells and rockets. Monitors still show projectiles.
radar_fcs.gui.intercept_hint.threatening: Hostile big cannon shells and rockets are shot down if their flight (CBC physics, until it hits blocks) passes closer than the threat radius to this computer, its cannons or friendly transponder zones. Friendly: fired by this computer's cannons, by computers of the same owner or team, or from friendly zones. Small ones (autocannons, machine guns, rocket pods) are not tracked.
radar_fcs.gui.intercept_hint.approaching: All hostile big cannon shells and rockets approaching this computer are shot down, even if they would miss. Friendly: fired by this computer's cannons, by computers of the same owner or team, or from friendly zones. Small ones (autocannons, machine guns, rocket pods) are not tracked.
radar_fcs.gui.intercept_hint.all: All hostile big cannon shells and rockets in reach are shot down wherever they fly. Friendly: fired by this computer's cannons, by computers of the same owner or team, or from friendly zones. Small ones (autocannons, machine guns, rocket pods) are not tracked.
radar_fcs.report.intercept_off: Interception: CBC Interception is not installed, projectiles are not shot down
radar_fcs.gui.wheel_hint: Mouse wheel: steps of 0.1 up to 1, then steps of 1; with Shift ten times more
radar_fcs.gui.mount_custom: Own targets for this cannon (otherwise the computer's common settings)
radar_fcs.gui.mounts_none: No cannons are linked to this computer (put a radar link on a mount).
radar_fcs.gui.mounts_hint_common: This cannon uses the computer's common target types and levels (Targets and Intercept tabs). Turn on own targets to set what it shoots at and what comes first: e.g. one autocannon only shoots down shells, another hits mobs.
radar_fcs.gui.mounts_hint_own: Own target types and levels of this cannon. The rest is common: whitelist and blacklist (the whitelist bypasses types), speed windows, IFF, threat filter, fire mode, drop and selection rules. A target designated on a monitor goes to all cannons.
radar_fcs.msg.excluded: Target excluded from fire: %s (middle-click again to restore)
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.pins_empty: No markers. Right-click the map on the Screen tab to place one.
radar_fcs.monitor_gui.pins_hint: Right-click the map to place a marker, right-click a marker to remove it. Markers are visual only and do not affect fire.
radar_fcs.link.overflow: Radar network %s is full: %s links, %s allowed — this one is inactive (each powered memory block adds 16)
radar_fcs.link.usage: Network connections: %s of %s (16 + 16 per memory block)
radar_fcs.tooltip.camera: Mounts on a wall, ceiling or floor. Joins a radar network with or without a radar link: right-click a radar link with the camera to tune it, like a Create Factory Gauge. A camera monitor of the network lets you look through it and aim the guns where it looks.
radar_fcs.tooltip.camera_monitor: Right-click: pick a camera of its radar network and look through it. Left-click: fire signal to all guns of the network (like redstone 15; hold for continuous fire). Shift: exit. Energy: 64 FE/t per camera in the network.
radar_fcs.camera.not_linked: This camera is not in the monitor's radar network
radar_fcs.camera.busy: Another player is controlling this camera
radar_fcs.camera.hint: Left-click: fire signal to all guns of the network (hold for continuous fire), Shift: exit
radar_fcs.camera_gui.title: Camera Monitor
radar_fcs.camera_gui.empty: There are no cameras in this monitor's radar network. Place a camera and connect it to the monitor with a radar link.
radar_fcs.camera_gui.hint: Press Enter to save the camera name. "Guns": which guns the camera controls (all by default); while you look through it, their auto-aim is paused.
radar_fcs.status.camera_self: camera is looking at its own gun: aiming paused
radar_fcs.tooltip.sight: Place it with the lens facing where you look. Sets which direction of the gun is aimed at the target; surrounding blocks do not matter. Without a sight the barrel of the gun's CBC mount is aimed. Outputs a redstone signal while the gun should fire (also with CBC mounts).
radar_fcs.tooltip.gun_link: Joins the parts of one gun — sight, drives and CBC mounts — into a gun network. Shift+right-click: gun settings (name, type, auto-aim, firing). Put the radar link on any part of the gun.
radar_fcs.sight.info: Sight: heading %s°, elevation %s°; drives %s, CBC mounts %s
radar_fcs.sight.no_rotators: No drives: connect the sight to them with gun links
radar_fcs.gun_link.not_linked: The gun link is not connected to anything
radar_fcs.gun_link.no_sight: The gun has neither a sight nor a CBC mount — the computer does not know what to aim
radar_fcs.gun_link.place_on_gun: A gun link goes on a sight, a gun drive or a CBC mount
radar_fcs.status.turret_no_power: no rotation on a gun drive
radar_fcs.tooltip.gun_drive: Like a Gearbox: input shaft at the back, output shaft at the front, but the output speed (-100% to 100% of the input) is set by the fire control computer. Drives anything: the bearing of a turning part, the yaw or pitch shaft of a CBC mount. Shift+right-click with an empty hand: yaw or pitch mode. Joins the gun with a gun link. Limit for each direction: slider on a side face (hold right-click), 1-360°, unlimited by default; yaw is measured from the gun's direction when the limit was enabled, pitch from the horizon.
radar_fcs.camera_monitor.no_energy: Not enough power for the camera monitor: needs %s FE/t (64 per camera)
radar_fcs.gun.title: Gun
radar_fcs.gun.name: Name
radar_fcs.gun.type.autocannon.hint: CBC autocannon ballistics; the fire signal is held while the gun is on target. With a CBC mount in the gun, ballistics and firing follow the mount.
radar_fcs.gun.type.medium.hint: Ballistics between autocannon and big cannon; fires in pulses. With a CBC mount in the gun, ballistics and firing follow the mount.
radar_fcs.gun.type.big.hint: CBC big cannon ballistics; fires in pulses (signal edge). With a CBC mount in the gun, ballistics and firing follow the mount.
radar_fcs.gun.type.custom.hint: Your own weapon: aims straight at the target, without lead or ballistics; the signal is held while on target.
radar_fcs.camera.tuned: Camera tuned to radar network %s — place it, no link needed
radar_fcs.camera.tooltip_untuned: Right-click a radar link to tune it to that network (no link needed for the camera)
radar_fcs.camera_gui.guns_empty: No fire control computers with cannons or guns in this monitor's network.
radar_fcs.camera_gui.guns_hint: Checked guns aim where this camera looks and fire on left-click; the others keep engaging targets on their own. Nothing checked — all guns. * — an assembled gun with drives.
radar_fcs.angle_limit.title: Rotation limit
radar_fcs.tooltip.flight_bridge: Points a Create: Flight Control autopilot at the radar network's target, like the Navigation Terminal. Place it on a Sable ship, add it to a radar network with a Radar Link and link it to the Flight Control Computer and the Forward Indicator with the Flight Control Tool Gun. Needs a Velocity Coupler (movement) and an Angular Velocity Coupler (turning) linked to the same computer: the bridge gives them targets and meanwhile switches off the Attitude and Altitude Stabilizers, the Distance Coupler and the Flight Control Terminal. Target: the one designated on a monitor, otherwise the fire control computer's target; it chases nothing else — with no target the ship hovers or flies an orbit. Right-click: settings — yaw, roll, pitch, "distance only" or "distance and altitude" mode with typed values, docking. A redstone signal pauses it (in "Docking: redstone" mode it sends the ship to dock)
radar_fcs.autopilot.title: Autopilot Bridge
radar_fcs.autopilot.mode.off.hint: The bridge only turns the hull to the target with the Angular Velocity Coupler; movement is left to other Flight Control blocks.
radar_fcs.autopilot.mode.distance.hint: The Velocity Coupler flies the ship to the target and keeps the set horizontal distance and the altitude at which the target was acquired. Stabilizers are switched off meanwhile.
radar_fcs.autopilot.mode.distance_altitu: The Velocity Coupler keeps the horizontal distance and the height above the target (negative — below it). Stabilizers are switched off meanwhile.
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.active: Flying the ship to the target
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.no_computer: Not linked to a Flight Control Computer (tool gun: bridge, then computer)
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.no_target: No target: designate one on a monitor (in "turn only" mode the bridge does nothing without a target)
radar_fcs.autopilot.summary: Distance %1$s blocks, speed up to %3$s blocks/s
radar_fcs.autopilot.summary_alt: Distance %1$s blocks, height above target %2$s blocks, speed up to %3$s blocks/s
radar_fcs.autopilot.indicator_linked: Ship nose: from the Forward Indicator
radar_fcs.autopilot.indicator_none: No indicator linked: the nose is the bridge's front face
radar_fcs.autopilot.axes_title: Deflections used to track the target:
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.computer_off: The Flight Control Computer is off or not in working mode
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.need_velocity: Needs a Velocity Coupler linked to the computer (movement)
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.need_angular: Needs an Angular Velocity Coupler linked to the computer (turning)
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.need_couplers: Needs a Velocity Coupler and an Angular Velocity Coupler linked to the computer
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.busy: Couplers are busy: a Navigation Terminal or a redstone proxy holds them
radar_fcs.tooltip.docking_controller: Automatic docking of Sable ships through the autopilot bridge (Create: Flight Control). With the Flight Control Tool Gun: right-click the controller, then Create Aeronautics Docking Connectors on the same structure — up to 8 facing the same way, all share the controller's number (right-click a connector again to remove it; Shift+right-click the controller to unlink all). Add it to a radar network with a Radar Link. "Port" role: next to the connectors ships dock to (ground, station, another ship); "plug" role: on the ship next to its own connectors. The plug takes the ship to the nearest free port with the same number and puts each of its connectors onto its own port connector, turning in advance (for up/down-facing ports also by heading); the Tool Gun highlights the controller and its connectors like Flight Control links. Controllers extend the connectors, the connectors lock on their own. Clearance distance — how far in front of the port the ship lines up for the straight approach; until it is on the port axis it keeps at least that far away and flies around the port (the larger of port and plug is used). While docked, the ship's Flight Control engines are off and its guns inactive. When to dock is set on the bridge
radar_fcs.docking.title: Docking Controller
radar_fcs.docking.role.port.hint: Docking port: ships whose plug has this number dock to its connector. Several ports may share a number — a ship picks the nearest free one. The connector extends by itself when the ship that reserved it comes close.
radar_fcs.docking.role.plug.hint: Ship plug: this ship's autopilot bridge (same network) takes it to a port with this number when it is time to dock (bridge setting). The ship's connector extends by itself on final approach.
radar_fcs.docking.connector_none: No connectors: Flight Control Tool Gun — controller, then connectors
radar_fcs.docking.pick: Controller selected: right-click docking connectors on the same structure (again to remove)
radar_fcs.docking.pick_lost: Controller selection lost — select it again
radar_fcs.docking.too_far: The connector must be on the same structure and within %s blocks
radar_fcs.autopilot.dock.off.hint: The ship does not dock by itself. Redstone pauses the bridge.
radar_fcs.autopilot.dock.no_target.hint: No target for 2 s — to the port with the plug's number; a target appears — undock. Redstone pauses.
radar_fcs.autopilot.dock.redstone.hint: Redstone on the bridge — go dock (no pause); signal off — undock.
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.dock_no_plug: Docking: no plug in the network on this ship
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.dock_no_connec: Docking: the plug is not linked to a docking connector
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.dock_no_port: Docking: no port with the plug's number in the network
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.dock_ports_bus: Docking: all ports with this number are busy
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.dock_waiting: Docking: waiting for the port to free up
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.dock_tilt: Docking: the plug cannot meet the port (they face at different angles)
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.docked: Docked: Flight Control engines off, guns inactive
radar_fcs.docking.facing: All connectors of a controller must face the same way
radar_fcs.tooltip.orbit_beacon: Orbit center for the autopilot bridge (Create: Flight Control). Add it to the bridge's radar network with a Radar Link; right-click to set the beacon code. A bridge with a code ("No target" tab, "orbit the beacon") circles the network's beacon with that code; without a code — the network's first beacon. It may sit on another ship — the orbit follows it. Radius, height and direction are set on the bridge
radar_fcs.orbit_beacon.goggles: Orbit center for bridges of the network
radar_fcs.autopilot.idle.hover.hint: No target — the ship holds where the target was lost, level, keeping its heading.
radar_fcs.autopilot.idle.orbit_point.hin: No target — the ship circles the point at the orbit speed.
radar_fcs.autopilot.idle.orbit_beacon.hi: No target — the ship circles its network's beacon (with the bridge's code); no beacon — it hovers.
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.idle_no_beacon: No target: no Orbit Beacon (with this code) in the network — hovering
radar_fcs.orbit_beacon.no_code: No code (a bridge without a code uses the first beacon of its network)
radar_fcs.orbit_beacon.hint: Add the beacon to the bridge's radar network with a Radar Link. A bridge with a code ("No target" tab, "orbit the beacon") circles the network's beacon with that code; a bridge without a code circles the network's first beacon.
radar_fcs.autopilot.orbit_code: Network beacon code (empty — the first one):
radar_fcs.autopilot.state.dock_layout: Docking: the ship's connectors do not match the port's (different number or layout)
radar_fcs.autopilot.orbit_facing.along.h: The ship faces where it flies along the circle (banks into the turn if roll is on)
radar_fcs.autopilot.orbit_facing.backwar: The ship flies the circle stern first
The nose always points at the orbit center — the ship circles it sideways
radar_fcs.autopilot.orbit_facing.outward: The nose always points away from the orbit center
radar_fcs.autopilot.orbit_facing.fixed.h: The ship keeps the heading it had and circles without turning
radar_fcs.ponder.tag.fire_control.descri: Fire control computer, links, aim controllers, monitors, cameras and guns
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.header: A battery: computer, cannon and radar
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_1: The Fire Control Computer aims Create Big Cannons and fires on its own. The cannon sits on a CBC mount or a compact mount from CBC: Firepower Components; big cannons, autocannons and addon guns all work
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_2: The mount needs aim controllers: yaw below it, pitch on its side. Feed rotation into the controllers, not the mount: shaft speed sets how fast the cannon turns
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_3: Targets come from Create: Radars radars: plane radar, radar bearing and others. Without a working radar in the network there is no fire (except a manually designated target)
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_4: The computer can stand anywhere. It needs 1024 FE/t of electricity; without power it sees no targets
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_5: Everything connects with Radar Links of one network, like Create Stock Links. Distance does not matter
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_6: The computer picks a target, leads it with CBC ballistics (charges, barrels, shell), turns the cannon and fires. Each shot refines the ballistics
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_7: It fires only when a shot from the current barrel position will hit and no friends or blocks are in the way
radar_fcs.ponder.battery.text_8: Right-click the computer for settings (see the next scene). Shift+right-click holds or allows fire; aiming continues
radar_fcs.ponder.computer_settings.text_: Right-click the computer to open its settings. Each computer has its own, stored in the block. Change numbers with the mouse wheel or the -/+ buttons (Shift for bigger steps)
Fire tab: fire mode. Single: one shot, then a pause. Automatic: fire while the shot will hit. Burst: N shots, then a pause in seconds. Shots are counted by projectiles leaving the barrel
Targets tab: what to engage: ships, players, mobs, entities (boats, minecarts, contraptions). Each type has a priority level 1-5 (higher first) and a speed window "from ... to ..." m/s

Lists tab: the whitelist is always engaged, regardless of types; the blacklist never. Entries: an id (minecraft:zombie), a tag (#minecraft:undead), a whole mod (create:*) or a player, ship or name-tagged mob name. 16 entries + 16 per Memory Block

Drop tab: when to give up a target: static ones (standing longer than the "standing time"; a short stop does not count), moving ones, or after N shots — each gun fires its own N shots. Saving the settings restores dropped targets

Pick tab: which target comes first: nearest, earliest, farthest, largest, smallest, fastest or slowest. "Switch to a higher priority target" and the switching rule: after N shots, after a time, when it stops, or never
IFF tab: a whitelist or blacklist of transponder codes — which transponders count as friendly
Intercept tab: shoot down big cannon shells and rockets (needs the CBC Interception mod). Threat filter: threatening (landing near friends), approaching or all hostile; "earlier impact first"
Guns tab: targets for a single gun — which types and levels it engages, e.g. one gun for ships, another for mobs
Status tab: a summary of radars, guns and their status, miss and barrel spread, targets. The "Assemble cannons" and "Disassemble cannons" buttons help with reloading and rebuilding
Shift+right-click holds or allows fire. Create's Engineer's Goggles show the same summary, a Display Link has a "Fire control targets" source, a comparator reads the target count
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_1: The Yaw Controller goes right below the mount (above a hanging one). Its shaft comes in from below
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_2: The Pitch Controller goes on the side of the mount, with its shaft on the far side
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_3: The controller turns the cannon by exactly the commanded angle. Speed works like CBC shafts: 0.0375° per tick for each RPM
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_4: 256 RPM gives 9.6° per tick (192° per second), 64 RPM gives 2.4°. For fast targets use 128-256 RPM
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_5: Load: 4 stress units per RPM. While the computer controls the mount, its own shafts are locked. The output half-shaft shows the cannon angle
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_6: Without a controller ("no aim controller") or rotation the cannon neither aims nor fires. Engineer's Goggles show the turn speed
radar_fcs.ponder.aim_controllers.text_7: Rotation limit: two boxes on the side of the controller, one per direction (hold right-click for a slider like the Torsion Spring). Yaw — left and right of the barrel's assembled direction, pitch — up and down from the horizon, 1-360°; the right end means no limit. Targets beyond the limit are skipped; with no others the cannon waits at the limit ("out of arc")
radar_fcs.ponder.network.header: Radar networks and the Memory Block
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_1: Computers, mounts, radars, monitors, cameras and gun parts connect only through Radar Links; nothing connects by range on its own
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_2: Place a link on a device. An untuned link starts a new radar network (its name, like "#3F2A", appears in chat)
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_3: Right-click a placed link with a link item to tune the item to its network; it glows. Next links join that network
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_4: All devices of one network are connected at any distance within a dimension. Looking at a link highlights its network
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_5: Right-clicking a link and Engineer's Goggles show the network name and how many computers, guns, radars and monitors it has. A device can join several networks with links on different faces
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_6: A network holds 16 device links plus 16 per powered Memory Block (240 FE/t). Each Memory Block also adds 16 entries to every list of the computer. Extra links report "network full"
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_7: A redstone signal of strength 15 disables a link; remove the signal to bring it back
radar_fcs.ponder.network.text_8: Shift+right-click in the air or the crafting grid resets the link item
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_1: Place monitors as a wall up to 6x6: it forms a single screen
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_2: Put a link on any screen block. The monitor draws a map of targets and radars of its network: the monitor is in the center, up points away from you, "N" marks north
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_3: On the map: friendly, threat, peaceful and inactive targets in different colors, targets under fire, radar beams and zones, transponders and range marks on the axes
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_4: Shift+right-click opens the monitor window. The Screen tab shows the same map: click a target to designate it, type the map size (16 — 1,000,000 blocks)
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_5: Computers of the network engage a designated target first, ignoring types and speed. The Targets tab lists targets to designate or clear
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_6: The View tab: display filters (friendly, threats, peaceful, inactive, radars, zones, transponders, pins), icons for each type — shape, color, size — and name labels: always or on hover
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_7: Pins: right-click the map in the window or use the Pins tab: coordinates, name and color. Pins are only drawn and do not affect fire
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_8: In the world: looking at a target shows its details, a middle-click excludes it from the computers (again to restore)
radar_fcs.ponder.radar_monitor.text_9: Power: 32 FE/t per screen block, fed into any block of the wall
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_1: The transponder marks friends: computers do not fire at anything in its zone or through it
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_2: Right-click opens the transponder screen. The name (up to 32 characters) labels the target and its monitor mark. The code (1-8 digits) tells computers whether it is friendly
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_3: Radius mode: a sphere of the set radius around the transponder; on a ship the zone moves with it
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_4: Ship mode: the Sable ship or contraption it stands on (bounds + 2 blocks); "ship and distance": the ship plus a set distance around. The default depends on where it stands
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_5: The Inheritance tab sets who in the zone is protected: players, hostile and peaceful mobs, ships, contraptions, projectiles, others. "Always" and "never" lists work like the computer target lists
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_6: The computer IFF tab holds a whitelist or blacklist of codes — which transponders are friendly
radar_fcs.ponder.transponder.text_7: Only the owner, their team and operators see and change codes. Power: 64 FE/t; without it the transponder protects nothing
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_1: A camera goes on a wall, ceiling or floor. Its head turns where you look through it and keeps its last position
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_2: Connect it with a Radar Link or without one: right-click a Radar Link (or a networked camera) with the camera item to tune it. Shift+right-click in the air resets it
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_3: The Camera Monitor (right-click) lists the cameras of its network. Rename a camera with Enter; "View" looks from the camera center
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_4: While you look, auto aim of the network guns pauses: they aim where the camera looks, up to 384 blocks, leading moving ships and entities
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_5: Left-click fires all controlled guns like redstone 15 (hold for continuous fire). Shift exits
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_6: The "Guns" button in a camera row chooses which guns it controls. The others keep tracking targets or follow another camera. Nothing checked means all guns
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_7: Looking at a controlled gun itself (or, from a camera mounted on it, at its own parts) keeps it still; left-click still fires
radar_fcs.ponder.camera.text_8: The monitor uses 64 FE/t per camera in its network. Walk away or exit and the guns go back to auto aim at once
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.header: A custom gun on Swivel Bearings
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_1: A custom Sable gun is built on Create Aeronautics Swivel Bearings. Yaw: a bearing facing up
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_2: The bearing is driven through its cog. A Gun Drive in yaw mode feeds it through cogwheels; the computer sets the drive output speed and direction
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_3: Select the rotating part with Super Glue. The bearing assembles it into a Sable structure once its cog gets rotation
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_4: On the rotating part goes a second bearing facing sideways for pitch. Glue its rotating part (the barrel) too; assemble the inner bearing first
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_5: A second drive turns the pitch bearing: shift+right-click it with an empty hand for pitch mode. Rotation can reach the rotating part through a shaft passing through the yaw bearing
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_6: The barrel can be any blocks. Place the Sight facing along the barrel: the computer aims the sight direction, so the shape does not matter
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_7: Gun Links on the drives and the sight join them into one gun (an untuned link starts a new gun, right-click a placed one to tune the item)
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_8: Put a Radar Link on any part of the gun: one link connects the whole gun. The gun's own structure is neither a target nor an obstacle
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_9: The computer learns the drive ratio and direction from how the sight turns; if aiming wobbles at first, it settles within seconds
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_10: When it is time to fire, the sight emits redstone 15 — wire it to your weapon. CBC mounts in the gun fire on command by themselves
radar_fcs.ponder.swivel_turret.text_11: Shift+right-click a Gun Link for gun settings. For a custom weapon pick its type: autocannon, medium, big (ballistics and signal kind) or "custom" — aims straight at the target without lead
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_1: The Gun Drive works like a gearbox: input behind, output in front (-100%% to 100%% of input). The computer sets the output. Here it turns the yaw shaft of the mount instead of an aim controller
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_2: Shift+right-click with an empty hand to switch the drive between yaw (↔) and pitch (↕)
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_3: The output can drive a bearing, gears or a mount shaft. The computer learns the ratio and direction by itself
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_4: Rotation limit: two boxes on the side of the drive, one per direction (hold right-click for a slider), 1-360°, the right end means no limit. Yaw counts from where the gun pointed when the limit was enabled, pitch from the horizon. The gun never turns through the forbidden arc — it goes the other way round
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_5: Gun Links join drives, mounts and sights into one gun
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_6: Shift+right-click a Gun Link for gun settings (shared by all its links). The name shows in the computer report and the camera monitor
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_7: The type sets ballistics and the signal for guns without a CBC mount: autocannon — the signal holds while on target; medium and big — pulses; custom — aims straight at the target without lead. With a CBC mount, ballistics come from it
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_8: Auto aim off: the gun aims only from a camera. Firing off: the gun aims but never fires by itself (camera left-click still works)
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_9: A link on a CBC mount also has "Main cannon": its barrel is aimed when the gun has no sight, and its ballistics are used
radar_fcs.ponder.gun_drive.text_10: The CBC mount of the gun fires on command; the computer does not lock its shafts. Put a Radar Link on any part of the gun
radar_fcs.ponder.flight_bridge.text_1: The Autopilot Bridge connects the radar network to Create: Flight Control. It goes on a Sable ship and exists only when Flight Control is installed
radar_fcs.ponder.flight_bridge.text_2: Add it to a radar network with a Radar Link. Its target is the one designated on a monitor of the network (own or Create: Radars), otherwise the one a fire control computer is tracking. It chases nothing else: with no target the ship hovers in place or flies an orbit (the "No target" tab)
radar_fcs.ponder.flight_bridge.text_3: Flight Control tool gun: right-click the Forward Indicator, then the bridge — the ship nose comes from the indicator. Without one, the nose is the front face of the bridge
radar_fcs.ponder.flight_bridge.text_4: Then right-click the bridge and the Flight Control Computer with the tool gun. Like the Navigation Terminal, the bridge flies the ship through a Velocity Coupler (movement) and an Angular Velocity Coupler (turning) linked to the same computer and switches off the Attitude and Altitude Stabilizers meanwhile
radar_fcs.ponder.flight_bridge.text_5: Right-click the bridge for settings. Deflections used to track the target: yaw — nose on its bearing, roll — bank into the turn, pitch — nose on its elevation; roll and pitch limits are typed. The bridge keeps disabled roll and pitch level. Turn and flight speeds are capped by the couplers' own limits
radar_fcs.ponder.flight_bridge.text_6: "Distance only": the ship closes in and keeps the typed horizontal distance to the target; other blocks keep the altitude. "Distance and altitude": also the typed height above the target. The speed limit is typed too
radar_fcs.ponder.flight_bridge.text_7: A redstone signal pauses the bridge (in "Docking: redstone" mode it sends the ship to dock). With no target the ship hovers or orbits — the "No target" tab. Engineer's Goggles show the target, the distance and the links
radar_fcs.tooltip.laser_designator: Shift+right-click a radar monitor to bind it. Hold right-click to aim (zoom, mouse wheel 2-10x, green beam); left-click while aiming — the target under the crosshair (mob, projectile, Sable ship) is designated on that monitor, like right-clicking its blip on the screen, and the computers of the network engage it first. Left-click or shift+right-click in the air: clear the designation. The target must be seen by the radars of the monitor's network.
radar_fcs.designator.bound: Designator bound to the monitor at [%s %s %s]
radar_fcs.designator.unbound: Designator is not bound: shift+right-click a radar monitor
radar_fcs.designator.no_monitor: Designator's monitor not found (broken, not loaded or in another dimension)
radar_fcs.designator.not_tracked: The monitor does not see this target: it is not on its network's radars or it is friendly
radar_fcs.tooltip.gun_bearing: Only with Create Aeronautics. Works like the Aeronautics swivel bearing: right-click with an empty hand to assemble the structure in front (glue rules) onto the bearing plate, again (or right-click the plate) to disassemble it back into blocks. Turned by its built-in cog ring meshing with cogwheels next to it (usually from a Gun Drive); a shaft passes through into the structure; a sequenced gearshift turns it by an exact angle. Lock mode on the side panel (with redstone): unlocked - the turning part spins freely. Unlike the Aeronautics bearing it damps inertia: the turning part does not overshoot or sway, even with a heavy barrel or a pitch bearing on it.
radar_fcs.bearing.not_assembled: Not assembled: right-click with an empty hand to assemble
radar_fcs.designator.aim_hint: Left-click: designate the target under the crosshair (in the air: clear); mouse wheel: zoom
radar_fcs.bearing.too_fast: Too fast! The ring slips above %s RPM
radar_fcs.bearing.same_sublevel: The bearing stands on its own turning part
